Millbrook Regional Medical Center Emergency Department - PROCEDURE / OPERATIVE NOTE Patient: KESSLER, DWAYNE T MRN: 4471-0382 DOB: 11/08/2025 Date of procedure: 07/29/2070 Surgeon: Dr. Alistair Penhaligon (locum) Assist: Marisol Quintanilla RN Dictated using voice recognition, Dictated but not read.
Pre-op diagnosis: Laceration, left brow and zygomatic region. Post-op diagnosis: Same. Procedure: Simple layered repare of facial laceration, 4.5 cm.
DICTATION BEGINS. This is a 44-year-old right handed gentleman who works part time as a linen delivery driver for Brightwater Linen Supply and presented this evening with a laceration to the left face. Patient name is Kessler, that is Kilo Echo Sierra Sierra Lima Echo Romeo, K-E-S-S-L-E-R, first name Dwayne, as in Duane, scratch that, D W A Y N E. He says he caught his face on a cabinet door at home. His sister Gwen, Gwendolyn Kessler-Hart, who drove him in, was somewhat more doubtful of that account and said so to the nurse, not to me, and social work has been asked to see him. I did not feel it was my place to press the matter in the middle of a repair but I have documented her comment.
The area was prepped with chlorhexidine and draped in the usual sterile fashion. One percent lidocaine with epinephrine was infiltrated, about 5 mils. The wound was irrigated with 500 ml of normal saline and explored; there was no foreign body and no bony step off to palpation. Deep dermal layer closed with 5-0 absorbable interrupted. Skin closed with 6-0 nylon, 9 interrupted sutures. Hemostasis was adequate. Patient tolerated the procedure well, there were no complications. Tetnus status was up-to-date per the registry, so no booster was given.
Plan: ibuprofin 200 mg tabs, two tablets every 6 hours with food for pain. Keep dry for 48 hours. Sutures out in 5 days (that would be 08/03/2070) with his PCP or back here. Return for redness, pus, or fever. Dispo home with sister.
Per the template: Patient <<PATIENT_NAME>> verbalised understanding. Interpreter: not required. Allergies: *** Note to Dr. Penn Allegan for signature.
